scope: standard ordinary battle MVP only; no insert Ultimate, extra action, follow-up, summon, revive, Limbo, Break, scripted terminal, boss replacement, or special resource

packets.scope: positive ordinary HealData for a living, valid target
packets.selected_model: At HEAL_COMMIT_BOUNDARY, apply the already-calculated non-negative heal amount to CurrentHP (property 10), bounded by MaxHP (property 1): new_hp = min(max_hp, old_hp + heal_amount); overflow = max(0, old_hp + heal_amount - max_hp).
ordering_constraints: Natasha Skill02 builds HealData after its FormulaType 4 calculation.
The canonical write occurs after this request event has settled and before ordinary action completion.
external_evidence: External 4.4.54 reconstruction provides the amount and target facts; it is not treated as a local proof of listener order.
local_evidence: real_skill_heal_boundary_30.json: real Natasha Avatar_Natasha_00_Skill02_Phase02 contains HealHP after DispelStatus; HealHP produces HealData and fires the event.
healdata_type_inspection_30.json: HealData exposes Result_HealAmount, Result_HealRealAmount, Result_OverflowHealAmount and healing ratios.
mvp_ability_component_type_31.json: TurnBasedAbilityComponent.DirectChangeHP has a positive branch; GetProperty, CheckPropertyBoundary and CurrentHP event paths are local objects.
assumptions: No heal listener in the supported fixture changes HP again between request dispatch and settled action.
Target is alive and is not protected by an unsupported no-heal/death/revive rule.
unknowns: The exact EventManager listener/consumer that commits positive HealData has not been named.
unsupported_cases: healing listeners whose result is observable before action settlement
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Do not route this through DirectDamageHP. Once the content evaluator emits a positive settled HealData amount, update the target HP with the stated clamp at HEAL_COMMIT_BOUNDARY and expose overflow separately.

packets.scope: ordinary player shared skill-point resource (the client calls this BP in SkillCharacterComponent)
packets.selected_model: A Basic/Normal action is legal without a positive BP cost and contributes its positive bp_add after use. A BPSkill is legal iff team_skill_points >= its positive bp_need. At RESOURCE_PRE_COMMIT deduct positive bp_need; at RESOURCE_POST_COMMIT add positive bp_add; clamp to [0, team_skill_point_max].
ordering_constraints: SkillCharacterComponent.UseSkill calls _DecBPBeforeSkillUse before ability execution and _AddBPAfterSkillUse after it.
external_evidence: Nanoka 4.4.54 Natasha 110501 has bp_add=1; 110502 has bp_need=1.
local_evidence: mvp_skill_character_component_type_31.json: IsSelfAllowUseSkill, GetAllAllowSkillIdxList, GetSPNeedBySkillIndex, SkillPointEntity, _DecBPBeforeSkillUse and _AddBPAfterSkillUse are recovered local methods/holder.
mvp_bp_pre_writer_xrefs_31.json and mvp_bp_post_writer_xrefs_31.json: both helpers are direct calls from UseSkill, with the decrement before and addition after the ability path.
assumptions: The standard MVP team skill-point cap is supplied by the BattleInitialState/content profile; no special BP source or cap modifier is enabled.
unknowns: UI failure-code taxonomy and special BP exceptions are not modeled.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Keep one shared team_skill_points field. Reject a BPSkill before it starts when positive bp_need exceeds it; commit cost before effects and gain after effects; negative/null Nanoka BP values mean no positive cost/gain, not a signed mutation.

packets.scope: ordinary actor energy (the local component calls this SP)
packets.selected_model: An Ultimate is legal iff actor.energy >= actor.energy_max. At RESOURCE_PRE_COMMIT deduct its energy_max. At RESOURCE_POST_COMMIT add the skill's positive sp_base energy gain and clamp to [0, energy_max]. Basic and Skill have zero energy cost in the standard scope and gain their positive sp_base after use.
ordering_constraints: SkillCharacterComponent.UseSkill calls _DecSPBeforeSkillUse before ability execution and _AddSPAfterSkillUse after it.
The standard MVP only observes state after the action effect settles; it does not permit mid-action Ultimate insertion.
external_evidence: Nanoka 4.4.54 gives Natasha sp_need=90 and skill sp_base values 20/30/5 for Basic/Skill/Ultimate.
local_evidence: mvp_ability_component_type_31.json: get_CurrentSPValue, get_MaxSPValue, get_CurrentSPFull, RegisterEnergyPoint and ChangeEnergyPoint exist on TurnBasedAbilityComponent.

mvp_skill_character_component_type_31.json plus mvp_sp_pre_writer_xrefs_31.json/mvp_sp_post_writer_xrefs_31.json: UseSkill calls _DecSPBeforeSkillUse before its ability path and _AddSPAfterSkillUse after it.
assumptions: No special energy type, extra max energy, energy lock, or on-hit energy listener is enabled.
unknowns: Exact listener timing inside an action is intentionally not claimed.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Store energy per actor, never in team_skill_points. Apply the pre/post boundary above, then expose only the settled result to the next ordinary actor.

packets.scope: ordinary eligible action list; no AV modification or insert action
packets.selected_model: At ORDINARY_ACTION_COMPLETED, set the acting entity's property 38 to UnitActionDelay(actor), advance every eligible actor by the selected pre-reset delay, stably order by remaining delay then deterministic entity key, and select the first eligible actor. UnitActionDelay is the local fixed-point ActionDelayDistance / speed(property 32) result; the standard MVP profile fixes ActionDelayDistance to 10000.
state_writes: all eligible property 38 values after elapsed-delay advance
ordering_constraints: Action effects and resource post-commit must settle first.
The recharge/reset is applied before the next ordinary actor is selected.
No supported listener may insert or advance an actor between these two MVP boundaries.
external_evidence: The standard HSR ordinary action-value convention uses ActionDelayDistance 10000; it is a reconstruction constant, not asserted to be a DesignData field.
local_evidence: turn_av_semantics_29.json: property 32 is speed, property 38 is remaining action delay; local ordering/advance and completion gates are recovered.
mvp_turn_based_game_mode_type_31.json: ShouldResetActionDelay, ResetAllEntityActionDelay and ResetEntityListActionDelay are real local scheduler methods.
mvp_reset_all_entity_delay_callback_31.txt: scheduler reset callback invokes TurnBasedAbilityComponent.get_UnitActionDelay for each entity.
mvp_get_unit_action_delay_31.txt: get_UnitActionDelay reads property 32 and divides ActionDelayDistance by it using FixPoint.op_Division.
assumptions: ActionDelayDistance is exactly 10000 for the fixed standard MVP profile.
No unsupported action-delay modifier changes the selected actor's reset delay.
unknowns: The complete native callback chain from every ordinary action completion to ResetEntityListActionDelay is not named.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Use fixed-point arithmetic. The standard profile must set action_delay_distance=10000. Do not select the next actor until effects, resource post-commit and this recharge/advance/order step are complete.

packets.scope: ordinary combatant death; no revive, fake death, escape, boss replacement or limbo
packets.selected_model: At DEATH_COMMIT_BOUNDARY after an HP mutation settles, an ordinary entity with CurrentHP <= 0 receives life_state=DEAD. DEAD entities are removed from ordinary action eligibility and ordinary target candidates.
ordering_constraints: HP write settles before life-state classification.
Life-state filtering happens before a subsequent ordinary action selection or terminal check.
external_evidence: Standard battle reconstruction treats zero HP ordinary combatants as dead; special death replacement is excluded.
local_evidence: mvp_target_filter_type_inspection_31.json: TargetQuery carries AliveStateMask and TargetFilterAliveState carries Mask.
mvp_target_alive_filter_evaluate_31.txt: TargetFilterAliveState evaluator removes candidates that fail its configured alive-state mask.

mvp_ability_component_type_31.json: _OnAbilityCurrentHPChangeEvent, _OnAbilityBeforeDying, CommonProcessOnLevelEntityDieOrEscape, DeathVersion, DeathSource and DeactiveActionStateKey_Die are local members.
assumptions: The entity is an ordinary combatant and no local special-death flag intercepts the zero-HP path.
unknowns: Exact native enum values/bitmasks for every AliveState are not needed by the MVP-derived life_state representation.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Represent ordinary life_state explicitly but derive it from settled CurrentHP in this scope. Immediately exclude DEAD actors from ordinary action and target enumeration; retain the entity record for replay/provenance.

packets.scope: Basic, Skill and Ultimate legality for ordinary player actors and ordinary targets
packets.selected_model: An action is legal iff actor life_state=ALIVE, it is actor's ordinary turn, the resource gate for its type passes, and its target set is nonempty after faction/alive/type filtering. Basic targets living enemies; healing/restoration Skill targets living allies; Ultimate target metadata selects living targets in its declared ordinary scope.
state_writes: none; returns legal action descriptors and legal target lists
ordering_constraints: Target filtering and resource gate run before RESOURCE_PRE_COMMIT.
Terminal state is checked before legal action enumeration; terminal battle has no legal ordinary actions.
external_evidence: Nanoka 4.4.54 skill type/tag supplies the static ordinary targeting intent, for example Natasha Basic SingleAttack and Skill/Ultimate Restore.
local_evidence: mvp_skill_character_component_type_31.json: IsSelfAllowUseSkill and GetAllAllowSkillIdxList are local legality entrypoints.
mvp_target_filter_type_inspection_31.json and targetconfig_type_inspection_30.json: target query, faction maps, alive/type filters, TargetType and MinTargetCount are local structures.
mvp_target_alive_filter_evaluate_31.txt: configured alive filtering removes invalid target candidates.
assumptions: Only canonical ordinary skill tags are compiled; no special-object, summon, body-part or forced-target policy is requested.
unknowns: TargetConfig discriminator 12's full generic join is not required for the supported normal tag set and is not claimed closed.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Compile a stable LegalAction descriptor containing actor, skill, cost/gain, target policy and explicit legal target IDs. Never infer target eligibility from UI text; use static tag plus faction/alive/type filters.

packets.scope: standard finite Stage Package; ordinary player and enemy combatants
packets.selected_model: At TERMINAL_CHECK_BOUNDARY after all HP/death changes from an action settle: if all player combatants are DEAD, result=DEFEAT; else if all active-wave enemies are DEAD, append the next exact Stage Package wave when one exists, otherwise result=VICTORY; else continue. Simultaneous player/enemy elimination is unsupported.
ordering_constraints: Wave spawn occurs only after the current active wave is fully dead.
Victory/defeat produces a terminal state before another ordinary actor is selected.
external_evidence: The exact 4.4.54 Stage Package provides stage/wave/monster ordering; 30113121 contains one configured monster entry 4014030.
local_evidence: mvp_turn_based_game_mode_type_31.json: IsAllDarkTeamDie, WaveMonsterBegin, WaveMonsterFinish, UpdateCurrentWaveCount, _OnEntityDied, get_IsLastMonsterWave, BattleResultState, CurrentWaveIndexInStage and WinFlag are local scheduler/result members.
mvp_ability_component_type_31.json: CommonProcessOnLevelEntityDieOrEscape establishes the local entity-side death boundary.
assumptions: Finite standard stage with no special score, scripted win/loss, infinite-wave or boss replacement rule.
unknowns: Exact client presentation/last-kill event timing is not modeled because it does not alter the supported terminal BattleState.
packets.DSH_implementation_contract: Stage compilation must preserve wave ordering. After each settled action, derive death first, then execute this terminal decision exactly; do not flatten all stage enemies into one roster.
